title: Reading an earnings report in 5 minutes
desc: Revenue, EPS and guidance against what was expected, and the earnings-day gap

cards.added: Feedback for options the board doesn’t show written for the Academy
cards.title: Record profit, price falls
cards.situation: Acme reports record sales and record profit. The share price falls 8% the next morning. Why?

visual.title: Acme · Q3
visual.label: Acme Q3: revenue $500M vs $520M expected, EPS $1.10 vs $1.20, both misses

options.feedback: The price already counted on a great quarter. It fell because the results came in below what was expected.
Price reacts to surprises, not results. A record that’s below hopes is a disappointment.
Record profits are good news. The price fell because they came in below what investors expected.

cards.work: Expected EPS $1.20, reported $1.10. A record, but $0.10 short.

cards.title: Three lines, in this order
cards.text: Every quarter, companies report results. Analysts publish forecasts first, the **[[earnings-estimate|expected]]** numbers. Check revenue and EPS against them, then the **[[guidance|guidance]]**: what the company expects next.

blocks.tip: A beat is above expected. A miss is below. The price moves on the gap.

cards.title: Read it in 5 minutes
cards.text: Northwind beat on revenue and on EPS. Then it lowered its sales forecast for next year.

visual.title: Northwind · Q2
visual.label: Northwind Q2: revenue and EPS beat, guidance $800M vs $880M expected

rows.note: Next year looks weaker: that moved the price.

cards.foot: Two beats, one cut, price down 6%. The market cares most about the future.

cards.added: Candle shapes drawn for the Academy around the board’s $50 close, $45 open and $48 stop
cards.title: Earnings day can jump the gap
cards.text: Results often come out when the market is closed. It closed at $50, then opened near $45, down 10%. A stop-loss at $48 fills at the first price, about $45.

chart.label: Closed at $50, results overnight, opened near $45 below the $48 stop

cards.rule: know the earnings date. Keep the position small or wait.

cards.added: Feedback for options the board doesn’t show written for the Academy
cards.title: Find the surprise
cards.q: Acme’s shares fell 12% after this report. Which line most likely caused it?

visual.title: Acme · Q4
visual.label: Acme Q4: revenue beat, EPS in line, guidance $1.1B vs $1.3B expected

options.feedback: Revenue beat the forecast, $300M vs $290M. A beat doesn’t usually sink a stock.
EPS matched what was expected, so it was no surprise. Guidance was the shock.
The outlook for next year came in well below what was expected. That was the shock.
A 12% move on results day has a reason. Look for the line that missed what was expected.

cards.added: Feedback for options the board doesn’t show written for the Academy
cards.title: Record, but…
cards.q: Analysts expected EPS of $2.00. Acme reports $1.90, its best ever. How will the market see it?

options.feedback: A record alone doesn’t move the price. Expectations do, and $1.90 is below $2.00.
Expectations set the bar. $1.90 is $0.10 short of the $2.00 expected, record or not.
Growth isn’t the test. The market compares with what was expected, and $1.90 is below $2.00.
Positive isn’t the bar. A beat means above what was expected, and $1.90 is below $2.00.

cards.headline: You can read an earnings report fast.
lines: Revenue and EPS: compare with what was expected.
Guidance about the future often matters most.
Price reacts to surprises, not results.
